sources.entry: LHA - Light Home Automation application that is fully extensible using Blockly, HTML or Lua. It includes extensions such as ConBee, Philips Hue or Z-Wave JS. MIT Lua

summary.one_liner: LHA is a light home automation application, written in pure Lua, that adds extensions for gateways such as ConBee, Philips Hue and Z-Wave JS, with automations scripted in Blockly, HTML or Lua.
summary.what_it_does: The lha engine manages extensions, scripts, things, a scheduler and a web server built on luajls. It records thing property values over time into time-based log files, which can be displayed as charts such as temperature history. Automations can be composed with Blockly block scripts or written in Lua, and custom web views can be built with HTML and Vue.js. It exposes a Thing Description JSON API following Web of Things. The README says it is a single-process application that needs no external dependencies and is around 5MB.
use_cases: enrich a Hue bridge with extra automations
record and chart temperature sensor history
send an SMS alert on intrusion
run home automation on a Raspberry Pi
how_to_run: Download the latest release for your target OS
Open the web interface in a browser
Go to the extension section to add and configure extensions
Provide an authorized user to use the ConBee or Hue bridge
notable: Scripts can be written in Blockly, HTML or Lua
Extensions for ConBee, Philips Hue and Z-Wave JS
Records device property values in time-based log files
Exposes a Web of Things Thing Description JSON API
Runs on small computers such as Raspberry Pi, Linux and Windows
caveats: Device support depends on editing extension JSON mapping files for new devices
ConBee and Hue bridges require an authorized user to be provided
Listed by awesome-selfhosted as MIT Lua; README does not describe further platform limits
